title: Trace drift & dashboard triage — weekly ops brief
content:
Meeting: Observability weekly triage — trace drift + dashboards
Date: 2026-12-10
Owner: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha, Daniel, Rosa, Ethan, Samir, Maya (brief check-in)
Duration: 45m standup-style + 25m deep-dive

Purpose: quick status on active trace/cost anomalies, dashboard query hotspots, and follow-ups from last sprint; make go/no-go decisions for two alerts and one backfill. This is intentionally informal — notes + action list.

Agenda:
- Quick pulses: any immediate page/alert?
- Trace drift summary and hypothesis triage
- Dashboards: panels causing large query/Redash load
- Cost telemetry: sampling changes & KV-cache implications
- Action items & owners

Notes:
1) Incident pulse
- No P1s. Small alert flapping on service inference-frontend traces (false positives from new sampling rule). Observed 3x alert noise between 09:00–11:00 PST on 12/09.
- Root cause hypothesis: sampling / tag normalization mismatch between proxy and client libs after the tagging change (OBS-1423).
- Temporary mitigation: mute noisy alert rule and add a short cooldown; Daniel and Rosa to verify suppression window doesn't hide real regressions.

2) Trace drift deep-dive
- Definition used: median span duration drift across last 24h vs baseline (30d). We saw a +22% drift in kv-store spans (read path) in region-us-west-2.
- Initial triage: coincides with a spike in prefix cache misses — possible evictions during pod churn (autoscaler event at 02:40 UTC).
- Telemetry notes: KV cache hit-rate metric (kv.cache.hit_rate) has new tags; dashboard panels referencing old tag names returned empty series and inflated the apparent miss-rate (visual drift). Ticket OBS-1589 opened to normalize tag mapping.
- Hypotheses ranked: 1) tag mismatch on metrics (high confidence), 2) real backend latency due to pod churn (medium), 3) model runtime variability (low).

3) Dashboard triage — panels causing heavy query load
- Redash/Metriq panels: three heavy panels identified: "inference:span-latency-by-node", "kv-cache-heatmap", and "trace-sample-rate-over-time". Together they run expensive group-by queries every 1m.
- Immediate recommendation: change refresh rate to 5m for heavy panels and add pre-aggregations (rollups). Samir to draft short patch for Metriq dashboard configs.
- Long-term: move heavy group-bys into precomputed materialized metrics via the telemetry pipeline (proposal in GH PR #87).

4) Cost telemetry and sampling changes
- We rolled out the new adaptive sampling (alpha) to 10% of traffic. Early data: per-token tracing cost down ~17% for sample group, but tail latency visibility decreased for low-frequency endpoints.
- Concern: some low-QPS customer routes lost debug traces — correlate with account-level SLO regression checks. Need to ensure canary has proper sticky sampling for those routes.
- Action: implement sticky sampling override for accounts with active debug sessions (short-term); product/CS notified.

5) Backfill / canary decisions
- Backfill for span-schema-v2 is queued (needs 72h run and impacts storage). We will run a 24h canary backfill on a single shard next week before full backfill. Rosa to coordinate shard selection.

Decisions made:
- Mute the noisy alert rule temporarily; implement 15m suppression window and revisit Monday (owner: Daniel).
- Change dashboard refresh for identified heavy panels to 5m (owner: Samir).
- Proceed with 24h canary backfill for span-schema-v2 on shard-3, scheduled Thu 12/16 (owner: Rosa).

Open questions / risks:
- Does tag normalization fix fully reconcile historical metrics used for baselines? If not, we need to recompute 30d baselines (costly).
- How do we balance sampling reductions vs developer debuggability for paid customers? (Product/CS alignment required)
- Storage spike risk during backfill — SRE involvement needed for temporary quota bump.

Action items (concise):
- OBS-1423: Fix tag normalization between proxy & client libs — Daniel — due 2026-12-14
- OBS-1589: Normalize dashboard metric mappings and mark panels for rollup work — Rosa — due 2026-12-15
- Metriq patch to bump refresh interval for three heavy panels + doc note — Samir — due 2026-12-11
- Implement suppression window for noisy alert and add runbook note — Daniel — due 2026-12-11
- Sticky sampling override prototype for debug sessions — Ethan — due 2026-12-17
- Shard selection & schedule for 24h canary backfill (span-schema-v2) — Rosa — schedule by 2026-12-12
- Open: request for SRE temporary storage quota bump for potential backfill spike — Aisha to open SRE request ticket by 2026-12-12

Follow-ups (who to loop in):
- Product/CS: confirm acceptable debug trace coverage & notify customers affected by sampling experiment (cc: Maya).
- SRE: scheduling window and storage quota checks for backfill (cc: Priya).
- Data-platform: quick feasibility check on computing fresh 30d baselines if tag normalization doesn't reconcile (cc: Li).

Quick wins for next week:
- Turn off 1m refresh on heavy panels (gains immediate CPU/DB savings).
- Deploy tag-normalization fix in telemetry agent (should resolve many empty-series issues).
- Add note in Trace Playbook about when to run canary backfills and preflight checklist.

Notes-to-self / rough TODOs (informal):
- Keep log of any suppressed alerts so we can reconvene if suppression masks real regressions.
- Try a short synthetic load on shard-3 in staging to estimate storage delta for backfill.
- Update runbook with example metrics to watch during canary (ingest-rate, storage-ops/sec, trace-ingest-latency).

References / links mentioned during meeting:
- OBS-1423 (Jira): tagging-change -> https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/OBS-1423
- OBS-1589 (Jira): dashboard-mappings -> https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/OBS-1589
- GH PR (telemetry rollups): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/87
- Trace Playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Trace+Playbook

Next meeting: 2026-12-17, 10:00 PST, quick check-in + backfill preflight review.

-- end of notes --
